purpose: Summarise an application against the published requirements for the Senior Backend Engineer role, to prepare a human hiring decision.
input_summary: One CV and cover letter (candidate reference APP-2026-0412), plus the published job requirements. No demographic data supplied.
output_summary: A structured summary of relevant experience with three requirement gaps noted, and a recommendation to proceed to a first interview.

data_recipients.transfer_mechanism: SCCs (Commission Implementing Decision 2021/914) under the Anthropic Commercial DPA
data_recipients.retention: Not retained for training; API inputs and outputs handled under the commercial terms

reasoning_summary: Each published requirement was checked against statements in the CV. Six of nine requirements are evidenced by named projects with dates. Three are not mentioned at all: Kubernetes operations, on-call experience, and formal mentoring. The recommendation to interview rests on the six evidenced requirements and on eight years of relevant backend experience; it does not rest on any assessment of the candidate as a person.

trace.summary: Summarise application APP-2026-0412 against the Senior Backend Engineer requirements
Loaded the candidate's CV and cover letter
Checked each of nine requirements against the CV: six evidenced by dated projects, three not mentioned (Kubernetes ops, on-call, formal mentoring)
Recommend proceeding to a first interview; flag the three gaps for the reviewer rather than treating them as disqualifying

sources.relevance: The only evidence about the candidate

confidence.rationale: Requirement matching from a CV is reliable for what is written and blind to what is not. Absence of a skill in a CV is not evidence of its absence in the candidate.

limitations: Only assesses what the candidate chose to write down. Unstated experience is invisible to this process.
Cannot assess communication, collaboration, or judgement — an interview does that.
Career gaps were not interpreted, since interpretation risks indirect discrimination.
Self-reported seniority in a CV was taken at face value and not verified.

human_review.reason: Recruitment screening is an Annex III high-risk use case and produces effects on individuals. No candidate is advanced or rejected on this output alone.
human_review.decision_notes: Agreed on advancing to interview. Removed the model's inference about 'likely culture fit', which was unsupported by the source material. Added a note to probe Kubernetes experience directly rather than treating its absence as disqualifying.

disclosure.disclosure_text: We use an AI assistant to summarise applications against the published role requirements. Every decision is made by a member of our hiring team. You can ask us how AI was used in your application at any time.

purpose: Answer a customer's billing question in the web chat widget and decide whether to escalate to a human agent.
input_summary: Customer asked why an invoice was higher than the previous month. Account reference and the last three invoices were retrieved from the billing system and supplied as context.
output_summary: Explained that the increase comes from two additional seats added on 3 July and the resulting mid-cycle proration. Offered a link to the seat management page. No escalation.

data_recipients.retention: Zero data retention on eligible endpoints; not stored at rest after the request completes

reasoning_summary: The invoice delta of €118.00 was matched against the line items. Two seats were added on 3 July at €59.00 each, prorated for the remaining 28 days of the cycle. The arithmetic reconciles to the cent, so no other cause needed to be considered. Escalation was not triggered because the question is factual, the answer is verifiable from the retrieved records, and no refund or credit was requested.

trace.summary: Customer asked why this month's invoice is higher than last month's
Read the last three invoices for the account
Matched the €118.00 delta to two seats added 3 July at €59.00, prorated over 28 days; reconciles to the cent
Answer factually and do not escalate; no refund or account change requested

sources.reference: billing.invoices where account_ref = ACC-88213, last 3 periods
sources.relevance: The invoice line items the explanation is built on
How mid-cycle seat additions are billed

confidence.rationale: The explanation is arithmetic over retrieved records, not an inference. The figures reconcile exactly.

limitations: Explains what was billed, not whether the seats should have been added — that is an account question the customer may still dispute.
Only the last three invoices were retrieved, so a longer-running pattern would not be visible.

human_review.reason: Informational answer with no legal or financial effect. No credit, refund, or account change was made. Escalation to a human is available in the widget at any point, and the customer was told so.

disclosure.disclosure_text: You are chatting with an AI assistant, not a person. Type 'agent' at any time to reach a human colleague.
